role: The revised consequence-first opening narration for the first ~45 seconds of the final film, and the identical copy used for the narrator A/B.

constraints.noMeasuredNumbers: No measured result appears in this copy. The evaluation numbers live on the frame, where a muted viewer recovers them.
constraints.noProofVocabulary: No HAC IDs, proof classes, hashes, receipts or decision enums in the first explanation.
constraints.noUnsupportedClaims: No 'safe', no 'prevents', no 'catastrophic', no universal claim against ordinary locking.
constraints.notAnAgent: Interlock is stated as a deterministic boundary, never as another reasoning agent (HAC-336 RC1 brief s4).

lines.spoken: A developer no longer runs one agent.
lines.note: Opens on the change, not on the product.

lines.spoken: Several workstreams now run at the same time, each making its own changes.
They touch different files, so they look independent.
But two changes can each be right on their own, and still be wrong together.
Checking each action on its own cannot see that. Local validity is not joint validity.
Interlock is not another agent. It is the deterministic boundary those actions pass through before shared state changes.
It reads revision-bound evidence from the repository, and decides whether they may proceed together.
Here is what that does on a small, fixed example.

pronunciation.note: Aliases are applied only to terms that actually remain in this copy. 'Interlock' is the only one; Gemini, ADK, MCP, WorkspaceJSON and Cloud Run do not appear in the opening and are handled later in the film, where RC1 already established that 'Google ADK' is spoken without its pinned version.
